title: OOM runway management: gated micro-quantization and tiered fallback choreography
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Short: Prevent and recover from GPU OOMs by implementing an OOM runway system composed of progressive token admission, a gated micro-quantization fast-path, and a tiered fallback choreography that gracefully degrades model fidelity or routes to cheaper model variants.

Background: Production serving at scale shows periodic OOM spikes when tail batches contain long-context requests combined with KV cache growth during heavy burst traffic. Existing mitigation strategies (eviction, batch contraction) reduce frequency but cause tail latency variance and unpredictable degraded outputs. This ticket designs and implements an end-to-end system that: (1) anticipates imminent OOMs using occupancy runway forecasting, (2) applies fast, bounded remediation (admit/thin tokens, apply micro-quantization per-request), and (3) executes a deterministic fallback choreography (reissue to compact variant or lower-fidelity model) with retry/hedging semantics.

Goals:
- Reduce OOM incidents by 90% on 95th/99th percentile workloads for known tail patterns.
- Keep P99 latency increase <= +20% for requests that are degraded.
- Ensure deterministic, auditable fallback decisions with observability hooks.

Non-goals:
- Global model swapping or long-running re-compilation. Not handling hardware faults.

High-level approach:
- Runway estimator: sliding-window occupancy predictor that signals 'runway_short' when projected memory exceeds threshold within Nms.
- Token admission controller: progressive token thinning (drop low-salience tokens in prefix) with per-request scoring and feedback from quality monitors.
- Gated micro-quantization: a fast quantization layer (FP16/8-lite) applied in-memory for select activations to free transient memory; reversible post-request.
- Tiered fallback choreography: deterministic ladder: same-model micro-quantized -> compact-variant (fewer heads/seq-len optimized) -> cheaper model variant -> retry with reduced max_tokens. Each step has backoff and hedging policy.
- Observability and audit: emit runway events, decision reasons, quality deltas and a unique fallback-id for tracing through Console and logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit/integration tests covering runway triggers, admission changes, quantization path, and fallback transitions.
- E2E load test demonstrating OOM reduction and acceptable latency/quality trade-offs on canary cluster.
- Console dashboard for runway events and per-fallback statistics.

Success metrics:
- OOM rate drop (95th/99th) > 90% in canary.
- False-positive degradation (requests unnecessarily degraded) < 1%.
- P99 latency increase for degraded requests <= 20%.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flags: runway estimator and fallback choreography behind runtime feature flag.
- Canary: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across regions; abort threshold: >5% customer-error increase or QoL metric degradation.

Monitoring & alerts:
- Alert: runway_short spikes > 5/min.
- Alert: fallback rate > baseline + 3σ.
- SLO impact dashboard slice for degraded requests.

Risks & mitigations:
- Quality regressions from token thinning: mitigate with conservative scoring and automatic rollback, and post-request quality evaluation harness.
- Quantization correctness/perf regressions: use micro-quant path on CPU/GPU with performance gates and fall back to safe path on anomalies.
- Complexity of tracing decisions: enforce a simple finite-state choreography and structured logs with fallback-id.
